A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original linear-regression experiments and Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct fine-tuning experiments on MMLU, including Figures 4–8 and Table 2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds empirical results for an auxiliary MMLU word-count task in Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: The linear-attention architecture, value-matrix fine-tuning strategy, training losses, minimal-update rule, and auxiliary-loss annealing remain unchanged. Separate query/key and two-head variants already appeared in v1 Appendix B.1.

E1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a task predicting which of four word-count bins contains an MMLU question, replacing its original answer label while retaining the input distribution. Existing linear-regression tasks and MMLU category coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments, including Figures 4–8 and Table 2, is unchanged. The added word-count task reuses the existing full and value-matrix fine-tuning strategies.

E3.justification: The added auxiliary experiment introduces controlled relabeling into 0–9, 10–19, 20–29, and at least 30 words, with a zero-shot base-model check and seven-shot evaluation of fine-tuned models. Previously reported splits, budgets, metrics, and model configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new word-count experiment tests whether the fine-tuning trend persists under a task modification intended to reduce confounding by prior task learning. Existing architectural variants and in-distribution versus out-of-distribution analyses are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: The existing MMLU protocol still reports three repeated evaluations, mean accuracy, and standard error. The added word-count results provide point accuracies without additional task-specific run counts, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Appendix B.2 adds 26.67% zero-shot accuracy for the base model on word counting and seven-shot accuracies of 47.76% for value-matrix fine-tuning and 46.57% for full fine-tuning. These are new-task results; existing figures and Table 2 values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, equations, theorem statements, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged apart from citation metadata. The added shared-query/key multi-head discussion explains applicability without introducing a new formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The core theoretical contributions remain the same. The abstract narrows the empirical-support claim from validating theoretical results to providing evidence consistent with their qualitative predictions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies the pretraining objective as an analytical surrogate, discusses prior instruction tuning as a limitation of the MMLU evidence, and limits task-similarity conclusions to the linear setting. It also clarifies multi-head applicability and acknowledges the small gap and limited settings of the new auxiliary experiment.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds a code-access link, and Appendix B.1 newly discloses that the existing two-head experiment does not share query/key parameters across heads. Existing hardware and fine-tuning hyperparameters are retained; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work positioning remain unchanged. Reference edits update formatting and bibliographic metadata, including the Matrix Cookbook citation, rather than introducing different research.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized rewrites to the abstract, pretraining explanation, Section 4.4, experiments, and limitations. Section 5 becomes Experiments, an Architectural Variants heading is added, and publication metadata is updated; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: All eight figures and both tables are retained. Figure 6 is relocated, Figures 7–8 and Table 2 move ahead of their appendix discussion, and Figure 1's caption corrects Theorem 4.1 to Corollary 4.1. The changes are limited layout and caption revisions.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the calibration of empirical claims and clarifies important applicability limits in Sections 3, 5, and 6. The auxiliary task provides a limited check on prior-learning concerns, while the code-access statement improves reproducibility information. These gains are modest: the core theory and existing results are unchanged, and the new comparison has a small gap without reported uncertainty.
